<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:重要無形民俗文化財]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q6573893]] Wikidata name: Important Intangible Folk Cultural Properties of Japan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:29, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} '''Important Intangible Folk Cultural Properties''' (重要無形民俗文化財, Jūyō Mukei Minzoku Bunkazai) are intangible cultural properties in Japan designated by the government as being of particular importance. These include customs related to daily life such as [[:en:Clothing|Clothing]], [[:en:Food|Food]], [[:en:housing|housing]], [[livelihoods]], [[:en:Faith|Faith]], and [[annual events]], as well as [[folk performing arts]] and [[folk techniques]] that have been created and passed down within communities. The system was established with the 1975 revision of the [[Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties]], with the first 30 properties designated on [[May 4, 1976]]. As of March 21, 2024, 333 properties have been designated.
== Background == The [[Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties]] defines intangible folk cultural properties as customs, folk performing arts, and folk techniques related to clothing, food, housing, livelihoods, faith, and annual events that are essential to understanding the transitions in the lives of Japanese people. Previously referred to as "intangible folk materials," these were areas of study in [[:en:Folkloristics|Folkloristics]] focusing on [[:en:folk traditions|folk traditions]].
The designation system emerged from growing awareness of the need to protect traditions passed down among ordinary people, which were increasingly endangered by rapid societal changes.
== Addition of Folk Techniques == In the 2004 revision of the Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties, the scope was expanded to include [[folk techniques]] in addition to customs and folk performing arts. Following this revision, the first designated folk techniques in 2006 included: * "Traditional Wooden Boat-Making Techniques of the Tsugaru Strait Region" ([[:en:Aomori Prefecture|Aomori Prefecture]]) * "Kazusa-Bori Well Digging Technique" ([[:en:Chiba Prefecture|Chiba Prefecture]]) * "Sinter Production Techniques of Beppu Myoban Onsen" ([[:en:Ōita Prefecture|Ōita Prefecture]])
== Designations by Region == Designations are organized by region, displaying the designated name, date, location, and preservation group. Properties recognized by [[:en:UNESCO|UNESCO]] as [[:en:Intangible Cultural Heritage|Intangible Cultural Heritage]] are marked with a ★.

[[:en:Aomori Prefecture|Aomori Prefecture]] * [[Enburi|Hachinohe Enburi]] (February 3, 1979 – [[:en:Hachinohe|Hachinohe]], [[:en:Nanbu|Nanbu]], [[:en:Hashikami|Hashikami]], [[:en:Oirase|Oirase]]) * [[:en:Aomori Nebuta Matsuri|Aomori Nebuta Matsuri]] (January 28, 1980 – [[:en:Aomori|Aomori]]) * [[Hirosaki Neputa Matsuri|Hirosaki Neputa Festival]] (January 28, 1980 – [[:en:Hirosaki|Hirosaki]]) * [[Iwaki-san#Oyama Sanke|Oyama Pilgrimage]] (January 21, 1984 – Tsugaru region) * [[Shimo-Kita Peninsula|Shimo-Kita]] Noh Dance (March 20, 1989 – [[:en:Mutsu province|Mutsu province]], [[:en:Yokohama|Yokohama]], [[:en:Higashidori|Higashidori]]) ; [[:en:Iwate Prefecture|Iwate Prefecture]] * [[:en:Hayachine Kagura|Hayachine Kagura]] ★ (May 4, 1976 – [[:en:Hanamaki|Hanamaki]]) * [[Motsuji#Ennen Performances|Motsuji Ennen]] (May 17, 1977 – [[:en:Hiraizumi|Hiraizumi]]) * [[Oni Kenbai|Nagai Daienbutsu Sword Dance]] ★ (January 28, 1980 – [[:en:Morioka|Morioka]]) ; [[:en:Miyagi Prefecture|Miyagi Prefecture]] * [[:en:Akiu no Taue Odori|Akiu no Taue Odori]] ★ (May 4, 1976 – [[:en:Sendai|Sendai]]) * [[Ogatsu Houin Kagura]] (December 20, 1996 – [[:en:Ishinomaki|Ishinomaki]]) ; [[:en:Akita Prefecture|Akita Prefecture]] * [[:en:Namahage|Namahage]] ★ (May 22, 1978 – [[:en:Oga|Oga]]) * [[Akita Kanto Festival]] (January 28, 1980 – [[:en:Akita|Akita]]) * [[Nishimonai Bon Odori]] ★ (January 21, 1981 – [[:en:Ugo|Ugo]]) ; [[:en:Fukushima Prefecture|Fukushima Prefecture]] * [[Soma Nomaoi]] (May 22, 1978 – [[:en:Soma|Soma]]) * [[Aizu-Tajima Gion Festival]] (January 21, 1981 – [[:en:Minamiaizu|Minamiaizu]]) * [[Tsurugaoka Hachiman-gu#Ritualistic Rice Planting|Tsurugaoka Hachiman Rice Planting Ritual]] (March 28, 2019 – [[:en:Kitakata|Kitakata]], [[:en:Aizumisato|Aizumisato]])
(Details for other regions continue similarly.)

These include customs related to daily life such as [[:en:Clothing|Clothing]], [[:en:Food|Food]], [[:en:housing|housing]], [[livelihoods]], [[:en:Faith|Faith]], and [[annual events]], as well as [[folk performing arts]] and [[folk techniques]] that have been created and passed down within communities. The system was established with the 1975 revision of the [[Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties]], with the first 30 properties designated on [[May 4, 1976]]. As of March 21, 2024, 333 properties have been designated.
== Background == The [[Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties]] defines intangible folk cultural properties as customs, folk performing arts, and folk techniques related to clothing, food, housing, livelihoods, faith, and annual events that are essential to understanding the transitions in the lives of Japanese people. Previously referred to as "intangible folk materials," these were areas of study in [[:en:Folkloristics|Folkloristics]] focusing on [[:en:folk traditions|folk traditions]].
The designation system emerged from growing awareness of the need to protect traditions passed down among ordinary people, which were increasingly endangered by rapid societal changes.
== Addition of Folk Techniques == In the 2004 revision of the Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties, the scope was expanded to include [[folk techniques]] in addition to customs and folk performing arts. <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:重要無形民俗文化財]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:重要無形民俗文化財]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ja:重要無形民俗文化財]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q6573893]] Wikidata name: Important Intangible Folk Cultural Properties of Japan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:29, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} '''Important Intangible Folk Cultural Properties''' (重要無形民俗文化財, Jūyō Mukei Minzoku Bunkazai) are intangible cultural properties in Japan designated by the government as being of particular importance. These include customs related to daily life such as {{ill|Clothing|en|Clothing|WD=Q11460|lt=Clothing}}, {{ill|Food|en|Food|WD=Q2095|lt=Food}}, {{ill|housing|en|housing|WD=Q1247867|lt=housing}}, [[livelihoods]], {{ill|Faith|en|Faith|WD=Q5410500|lt=Faith}}, and [[annual events]], as well as [[folk performing arts]] and [[folk techniques]] that have been created and passed down within communities. The system was established with the 1975 revision of the [[Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties]], with the first 30 properties designated on [[May 4, 1976]]. As of March 21, 2024, 333 properties have been designated.
== Background == The [[Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties]] defines intangible folk cultural properties as customs, folk performing arts, and folk techniques related to clothing, food, housing, livelihoods, faith, and annual events that are essential to understanding the transitions in the lives of Japanese people. Previously referred to as "intangible folk materials," these were areas of study in [[:en:Folkloristics|Folkloristics]] focusing on [[:en:folk traditions|folk traditions]].
The designation system emerged from growing awareness of the need to protect traditions passed down among ordinary people, which were increasingly endangered by rapid societal changes.
== Addition of Folk Techniques == In the 2004 revision of the Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties, the scope was expanded to include [[folk techniques]] in addition to customs and folk performing arts. Following this revision, the first designated folk techniques in 2006 included: * "Traditional Wooden Boat-Making Techniques of the Tsugaru Strait Region" ({{ill|Aomori Prefecture|en|Aomori Prefecture|WD=Q71699|lt=Aomori Prefecture}}) * "Kazusa-Bori Well Digging Technique" ({{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|WD=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}) * "Sinter Production Techniques of Beppu Myoban Onsen" ({{ill|Ōita Prefecture|en|Ōita Prefecture|WD=Q133924|lt=Ōita Prefecture}})
== Designations by Region == Designations are organized by region, displaying the designated name, date, location, and preservation group. Properties recognized by {{ill|UNESCO|en|UNESCO|WD=Q7809|lt=UNESCO}} as [[:en:Intangible Cultural Heritage|Intangible Cultural Heritage]] are marked with a ★.
=== Hokkaido and Tohoku Region === ; [[:en:Hokkaidō|Hokkaidō]] * [[Ainu Culture#Traditional Revitalization|Ainu Traditional Dance]] ★ (January 21, 1984 – various locations in Hokkaido) * [[Matsumae Kagura]] (March 8, 2018 – various locations in Hokkaido) ; {{ill|Aomori Prefecture|en|Aomori Prefecture|WD=Q71699|lt=Aomori Prefecture}} * [[Enburi|Hachinohe Enburi]] (February 3, 1979 – {{ill|Hachinohe|en|Hachinohe|WD=Q191914|lt=Hachinohe}}, {{ill|Nanbu|en|Nanbu|WD=Q1208539|lt=Nanbu}}, {{ill|Hashikami|en|Hashikami|WD=Q1349010|lt=Hashikami}}, {{ill|Oirase|en|Oirase|WD=Q1349124|lt=Oirase}}) * {{ill|Aomori Nebuta Matsuri|en|Aomori Nebuta Matsuri|WD=Q862407|lt=Aomori Nebuta Matsuri}} (January 28, 1980 – {{ill|Aomori|en|Aomori|WD=Q146790|lt=Aomori}}) * [[Hirosaki Neputa Matsuri|Hirosaki Neputa Festival]] (January 28, 1980 – {{ill|Hirosaki|en|Hirosaki|WD=Q194087|lt=Hirosaki}}) * [[Iwaki-san#Oyama Sanke|Oyama Pilgrimage]] (January 21, 1984 – Tsugaru region) * [[Shimo-Kita Peninsula|Shimo-Kita]] Noh Dance (March 20, 1989 – [[:en:Mutsu province|Mutsu province]], {{ill|Yokohama|en|Yokohama|WD=Q38283|lt=Yokohama}}, [[:en:Higashidori|Higashidori]]) ; {{ill|Iwate Prefecture|en|Iwate Prefecture|WD=Q48326|lt=Iwate Prefecture}} * [[:en:Hayachine Kagura|Hayachine Kagura]] ★ (May 4, 1976 – [[:en:Hanamaki|Hanamaki]]) * [[Motsuji#Ennen Performances|Motsuji Ennen]] (May 17, 1977 – {{ill|Hiraizumi|en|Hiraizumi|WD=Q1203004|lt=Hiraizumi}}) * [[Oni Kenbai|Nagai Daienbutsu Sword Dance]] ★ (January 28, 1980 – {{ill|Morioka|en|Morioka|WD=Q200077|lt=Morioka}}) ; {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|en|Miyagi Prefecture|WD=Q47896|lt=Miyagi Prefecture}} * {{ill|Akiu no Taue Odori|en|Akiu no Taue Odori|WD=Q2829083|lt=Akiu no Taue Odori}} ★ (May 4, 1976 – {{ill|Sendai|en|Sendai|WD=Q46747|lt=Sendai}}) * [[Ogatsu Houin Kagura]] (December 20, 1996 – {{ill|Ishinomaki|en|Ishinomaki|WD=Q270814|lt=Ishinomaki}}) ; {{ill|Akita Prefecture|en|Akita Prefecture|WD=Q81863|lt=Akita Prefecture}} * {{ill|Namahage|en|Namahage|WD=Q1133889|lt=Namahage}} ★ (May 22, 1978 – {{ill|Oga|en|Oga|WD=Q3880124|lt=Oga}}) * [[Akita Kanto Festival]] (January 28, 1980 – {{ill|Akita|en|Akita|WD=Q1872285|lt=Akita}}) * [[Nishimonai Bon Odori]] ★ (January 21, 1981 – {{ill|Ugo|en|Ugo|WD=Q2474009|lt=Ugo}}) ; {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|en|Fukushima Prefecture|WD=Q71707|lt=Fukushima Prefecture}} * [[Soma Nomaoi]] (May 22, 1978 – {{ill|Soma|en|Soma|WD=Q226058|lt=Soma}}) * [[Aizu-Tajima Gion Festival]] (January 21, 1981 – {{ill|Minamiaizu|en|Minamiaizu|WD=Q1205058|lt=Minamiaizu}}) * [[Tsurugaoka Hachiman-gu#Ritualistic Rice Planting|Tsurugaoka Hachiman Rice Planting Ritual]] (March 28, 2019 – {{ill|Kitakata|en|Kitakata|WD=Q6417754|lt=Kitakata}}, {{ill|Aizumisato|en|Aizumisato|WD=Q1205357|lt=Aizumisato}})
(Details for other regions continue similarly.)
== Related Articles == * {{ill|Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q858308|lt=Cultural Property (Japan)}} * [[:en:folk traditions|folk traditions]] * [[:en:Intangible Cultural Heritage|Intangible Cultural Heritage]]

'''Important Intangible Folk Cultural Properties''' (重要無形民俗文化財, Jūyō Mukei Minzoku Bunkazai) are intangible cultural properties in Japan designated by the government as being of particular importance. These include customs related to daily life such as {{ill|Clothing|en|Clothing|WD=Q11460|lt=Clothing}}, {{ill|Food|en|Food|WD=Q2095|lt=Food}}, {{ill|housing|en|housing|WD=Q1247867|lt=housing}}, [[livelihoods]], {{ill|Faith|en|Faith|WD=Q5410500|lt=Faith}}, and [[annual events]], as well as [[folk performing arts]] and [[folk techniques]] that have been created and passed down within communities. The system was established with the 1975 revision of the [[Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties]], with the first 30 properties designated on [[May 4, 1976]]. As of March 21, 2024, 333 properties have been designated.
== Background == The [[Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties]] defines intangible folk cultural properties as customs, folk performing arts, and folk techniques related to clothing, food, housing, livelihoods, faith, and annual events that are essential to understanding the transitions in the lives of Japanese people. Previously referred to as "intangible folk materials," these were areas of study in [[:en:Folkloristics|Folkloristics]] focusing on [[:en:folk traditions|folk traditions]].
The designation system emerged from growing awareness of the need to protect traditions passed down among ordinary people, which were increasingly endangered by rapid societal changes.
== Addition of Folk Techniques == In the 2004 revision of the Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties, the scope was expanded to include [[folk techniques]] in addition to customs and folk performing arts. Following this revision, the first designated folk techniques in 2006 included: * "Traditional Wooden Boat-Making Techniques of the Tsugaru Strait Region" ({{ill|Aomori Prefecture|en|Aomori Prefecture|WD=Q71699|lt=Aomori Prefecture}}) * "Kazusa-Bori Well Digging Technique" ({{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|WD=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}) * "Sinter Production Techniques of Beppu Myoban Onsen" ({{ill|Ōita Prefecture|en|Ōita Prefecture|WD=Q133924|lt=Ōita Prefecture}})
== Designations by Region == Designations are organized by region, displaying the designated name, date, location, and preservation group. Properties recognized by {{ill|UNESCO|en|UNESCO|WD=Q7809|lt=UNESCO}} as [[:en:Intangible Cultural Heritage|Intangible Cultural Heritage]] are marked with a ★.

'''Important Intangible Folk Cultural Properties''' (重要無形民俗文化財, Jūyō Mukei Minzoku Bunkazai) are intangible cultural properties in Japan designated by the government as being of particular importance. These include customs related to daily life such as {{ill|Clothing|en|Clothing|WD=Q11460|lt=Clothing|1=Clothing}}, {{ill|Food|en|Food|WD=Q2095|lt=Food|1=Food}}, {{ill|housing|en|housing|WD=Q1247867|lt=housing|1=Housing}}, [[livelihoods]], {{ill|Faith|en|Faith|WD=Q5410500|lt=Faith|1=Faith}}, and [[annual events]], as well as [[folk performing arts]] and [[folk techniques]] that have been created and passed down within communities. The system was established with the 1975 revision of the [[Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties]], with the first 30 properties designated on [[May 4, 1976]]. As of March 21, 2024, 333 properties have been designated.
== Background == The [[Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties]] defines intangible folk cultural properties as customs, folk performing arts, and folk techniques related to clothing, food, housing, livelihoods, faith, and annual events that are essential to understanding the transitions in the lives of Japanese people. Previously referred to as "intangible folk materials," these were areas of study in [[:en:Folkloristics|Folkloristics]] focusing on [[:en:folk traditions|folk traditions]].
The designation system emerged from growing awareness of the need to protect traditions passed down among ordinary people, which were increasingly endangered by rapid societal changes.
== Addition of Folk Techniques == In the 2004 revision of the Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties, the scope was expanded to include [[folk techniques]] in addition to customs and folk performing arts. Following this revision, the first designated folk techniques in 2006 included: * "Traditional Wooden Boat-Making Techniques of the Tsugaru Strait Region" ({{ill|Aomori Prefecture|en|Aomori Prefecture|WD=Q71699|lt=Aomori Prefecture|1=Aomori Prefecture}}) * "Kazusa-Bori Well Digging Technique" ({{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|WD=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture|1=Chiba Prefecture}}) * "Sinter Production Techniques of Beppu Myoban Onsen" ({{ill|Ōita Prefecture|en|Ōita Prefecture|WD=Q133924|lt=Ōita Prefecture|1=Ōita Prefecture}})
== Designations by Region == Designations are organized by region, displaying the designated name, date, location, and preservation group. Properties recognized by {{ill|UNESCO|en|UNESCO|WD=Q7809|lt=UNESCO|1=UNESCO}} as [[:en:Intangible Cultural Heritage|Intangible Cultural Heritage]] are marked with a ★.
